items.title: The One Dollar Counterfeiter
items.author: cainxinth
items.summary: Emerich Juettner was an Austrian-American counterfeiter who printed one-dollar bills for nearly a decade. He was eventually caught in 1948 and became a folk hero. The case was the most expensive in Secret Service history.

items.title: Gemini API File Search is now multimodal
items.author: gmays
items.summary: The Gemini API File Search tool now supports multimodal retrieval, enhancing its ability to process and retrieve data from multiple formats. This update includes custom metadata and page-level citations. The change was announced in May 2026.

items.title: Internet Archive Switzerland
items.author: hggh
items.summary: Internet Archive Switzerland is a non-profit foundation based in St. Gallen, Switzerland, dedicated to universal access to all knowledge. It partners with the University of St. Gallen for AI preservation and aims to prevent knowledge loss. Founded in 2026, it aligns with global Internet Archive initiatives.

items.title: Debian must ship reproducible packages
items.author: robalni
items.summary: Debian aims for reproducible packages, and as of 2026, 83% of its main packages meet this standard. Reproducible builds ensure identical package builds from the same source code. This policy enhances security and reliability.

items.title: Making your own programming language is easier than you think (but also harder)
items.author: ibobev
items.summary: Creating your own programming language is challenging but achievable; it requires significant effort to complete and polish. Many find the initial stages easier than the final refinement. Lua is often cited as a good starting point due to its sandboxing capabilities.

items.title: A recent experience with ChatGPT 5.5 Pro
items.author: _alternator_
items.summary: GPT-5.5 Pro is noted for its advanced capabilities in complex, multi-step tasks and superior writing quality. Users report mixed experiences, with some praising its power and others noting limitations in token usage. This model represents a significant step forward in AI performance.

items.title: LLMs corrupt your documents when you delegate
items.author: rbanffy
items.summary: Large language models can introduce errors when editing documents, leading to silent corruption. Current LLMs are unreliable for delegated document editing tasks. Benchmarks show significant issues with document integrity when using LLMs.

items.title: The first microcomputer: The transfluxor-powered Arma Micro Computer from 1962
items.author: rsecora
items.summary: The Arma Micro Computer, released in 1962, was an early minicomputer with a bit-serial architecture and transfluxor-based memory. It weighed 20 pounds and was designed for space applications. The Apple I, released in 1976, is often considered a significant microcomputer, but the Arma predates it.

items.title: EU Parliamentary Research Service calls VPNs "a loophole that needs closing"
items.author: muse900
items.summary: The EU Parliamentary Research Service warns that VPNs are used to bypass age verification, calling it a loophole needing closure. The EPRS suggests future EU cybersecurity updates may target this issue. This aligns with broader efforts to enforce child safety online.

items.title: Sparse Cholesky Elimination Tree
items.author: selimthegrim
items.summary: Sparse Cholesky Elimination Tree is a method for efficiently factorizing sparse matrices using elimination trees to determine the structure of the Cholesky factor. It leverages the elimination tree to reduce computational complexity. This method is faster than traditional approaches for sparse matrices.

items.title: The hypocrisy of cyberlibertarianism
items.author: ColinWright
items.summary: Cyberlibertarianism's hypocrisy lies in advocating for internet freedom while often supporting censorship and surveillance. Critics argue this contradicts its core principles. This tension highlights a fundamental conflict within the movement.

items.title: Using Claude Code: The unreasonable effectiveness of HTML
items.author: pretext
items.summary: HTML's effectiveness in generating rich, interactive content makes it a preferred output format for AI like Claude Code. It supports complex features like SVG diagrams and interactive widgets. This enhances user experience and document navigation.

items.title: Meta's embrace of AI is making its employees miserable
items.author: JumpCrisscross
items.summary: Meta's focus on AI has led to employee anxiety and discontent due to potential layoffs and increased AI integration. The company plans to cut 10% of its staff. Employees are reportedly unhappy with the AI push.

items.title: Mythical Man Month
items.author: ingve
items.summary: "The Mythical Man-Month" is a seminal book on software engineering by Fred Brooks, emphasizing that adding more people to a late software project does not speed it up and that communication overhead increases with team size. It highlights the importance of maintaining conceptual integrity in large projects.

items.title: OpenAI’s WebRTC problem
items.author: atgctg
items.summary: WebRTC is inefficient for voice AI due to its conferencing design, causing delays and poor audio quality. Alternatives are preferred. OpenAI faced significant issues with WebRTC.

items.title: France moves to break encrypted messaging
items.author: Cider9986
items.summary: France's parliament has endorsed breaking encryption for messaging apps like WhatsApp and Signal. This move aims to give intelligence services access to encrypted communications. Critics argue this undermines privacy protections.

items.title: Google broke reCAPTCHA for de-googled Android users
items.author: anonymousiam
items.text:
Related: Google Cloud fraud defense, the next evolution of reCAPTCHA - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48039362

also: Google Cloud Fraud Defence is just WEI repackaged - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48063199
items.summary: Google's reCAPTCHA now requires Google Play Services for verification, affecting de-Googled Android users. This means users must run Google's proprietary software to prove they are human. It forces users to transmit data to Google's servers.

items.title: MCP for sandboxed, reproducible envs for agentic-first coding workflows
items.author: anionyt
items.summary: MCP provides sandboxed, reproducible environments for agentic-first coding workflows, enhancing AI engine interactions and debugging. It supports interactive REPL-like loops for tuning and workflow adjustments. GitHub also offers sandbox configurations for these workflows.

items.title: Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Information Retrieval
items.author: CharlesW
items.summary: Superintelligent Retrieval Agent (SIRA) compresses multi-round search into a single retrieval action, outperforming dense retrievers and multi-round agents. SIRA uses LLM cognition and corpus statistics for efficient, interpretable search. SIRA achieves superior performance on benchmarks without training.

items.title: America's carpet capital: an empire and its toxic legacy
items.author: rawgabbit
items.summary: Georgia is known as America's carpet capital, but its industry has left a toxic legacy due to the use of forever chemicals that polluted water and land. The environmental damage has raised significant health concerns.

items.title: AI is breaking two vulnerability cultures
items.author: speckx
items.summary: AI is disrupting traditional security practices by rapidly identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities, reducing time-to-exploitation to minutes. This shift challenges existing vulnerability cultures. The new AI-driven approach emphasizes continuous, automated discovery.

items.title: Getting arrested in Japan
items.author: bane
items.summary: In Japan, you can be detained for up to 23 days without charge if suspected of a crime. Formal arrest follows this period. Legal counsel can be accessed after arrest.

items.title: The ROKR wooden typewriter: a closer look
items.author: speckx
items.summary: The ROKR wooden typewriter is a functional, handcrafted device with moving keys and an ink ribbon. It gained attention for its unique design and nostalgic appeal. It was showcased in various online forums and blogs.

items.title: Teaching Claude Why
items.author: pretext
items.summary: I am an AI system built by a team of inventors at Amazon. I assist with various tasks without revealing specific identities. I provide concise, factual responses.
